title: A Study to Investigate Immunogenicity and Safety of mRNA-1273.262 in Individuals ≥6 Months to <12 Years With Risk Factors for Severe COVID-19
official: A Phase 3b/4, Open-label, Single-Arm Study to Evaluate the Safety and Immunogenicity of mRNA-1273.262 in Individuals ≥6 Months to <12 Years With Risk Factors for Severe COVID-19
summary: Evaluates the safety and immunogenicity of mRNA-1273 formulation in individuals aged ≥6 months to \<12 years
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participant is male or female between ≥6 months to \<12 years of age (calculated from date of birth) at the time of signing the informed consent/assent with at least 1 risk factor for severe outcomes from COVID-19
* Participant's parent(s)/LAR(s) demonstrate adequate understanding of the study requirements and are willing, and physically able, to comply with protocol-mandated follow-up, including all procedures
* Female participants of nonchildbearing potential may be enrolled in the study. Nonchildbearing potential is defined as premenarche.

Special inclusion criteria for female participants who have reached menarche:

\- Female participants who have reached menarche may be enrolled in the study if all of the following criteria are fulfilled:

* Has a negative highly sensitive pregnancy test (urine or serum) as required by local regulations within 24 hours before the study vaccine.
* Is not currently chest/breastfeeding.
* Has been using a highly effective contraceptive method as described or has abstained from all activities that could lead to pregnancy for at least 28 days prior to the study injection (Day 1).
* Has agreed to continue adequate contraception through EOS.

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of anaphylaxis or severe hypersensitivity reaction requiring medical intervention after receipt of any mRNA vaccine or therapeutic or any components of an mRNA vaccine or therapeutic.
* History of SARS-CoV-2 infection within 3 months prior to enrollment.
* Acutely ill or febrile within 72 hours prior to or at the Screening Visit or Day 1.
* History of a diagnosis or condition that, in the judgment of the Investigator, is clinically unstable, or may affect participant safety, assessment of study endpoints, assessment of immune response, or adherence to study procedures
* Has undergone a surgical procedure within 28 days prior to Day 1 or is scheduled to undergo a surgical procedure within 1 month after study vaccine
* Known to have congenital or acquired immunodeficiency (including human immunodeficiency virus \[HIV\] infection), known or suspected impairment of immunological function, immunosuppressive condition, asplenia, or recurrent severe infections
* Receipt of any COVID-19 vaccine within 3 months prior to enrollment
* Receipt of any nonstudy vaccination within 14 days (28 days for live (vaccines) prior to study vaccine or plans to receive a nonstudy vaccine through 14 days after administration of study vaccine - Received systemic immunosuppressive treatment, including long-acting biological therapies that affect immune responses (eg, infliximab), within 180 days prior to Day 1 or plans to do so during the study

Additional criteria may apply.
